_metadata.law_reference: Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 (No. 22 of 2023)
_metadata.gazette_reference: The Gazette of India Extraordinary, Part II Section 1, No. 25, August 11, 2023
_metadata.disclaimer: This knowledge base provides automated compliance guidance based on DPDPA 2023. It is not legal advice. All assessments are heuristic starting points for compliance review. Consult qualified privacy counsel for definitive compliance determinations.
key_corrections_from_gdpr: DPDPA 2023 does NOT define a fixed list of special category data unlike GDPR Article 9
DPDPA Section 9 specifically governs children's data (under 18) — not a general sensitive category list
All personal data is governed by Sections 4, 5, 6, 7, 8 regardless of type
DPDPA has no legitimate interest basis — Section 7 lists exhaustive legitimate uses only
Consent must be free, specific, informed, unconditional and unambiguous per Section 6(1)

_violation_flags_reference.PURPOSE_LIMITATION_VIOLATION: Data used for purpose other than declared consent basis — Section 6(1)
_violation_flags_reference.NO_CONSENT_MECHANISM: No documented consent collected before processing — Section 6
_violation_flags_reference.NO_NOTICE_PROVIDED: No notice given to Data Principal before consent — Section 5
_violation_flags_reference.DATA_MINIMISATION_VIOLATION: Data collected exceeds what stated purpose requires — Section 6(1)
_violation_flags_reference.RETENTION_VIOLATION: Data held beyond stated purpose or legal requirement — Section 8(7)
_violation_flags_reference.NO_ERASURE_MECHANISM: No mechanism for Data Principal to request erasure — Section 12(3)
_violation_flags_reference.NO_GRIEVANCE_MECHANISM: No grievance redressal mechanism established — Section 8(10) and Section 13
_violation_flags_reference.SECURITY_SAFEGUARDS_MISSING: Inadequate technical/organisational security measures — Section 8(4) and 8(5)
_violation_flags_reference.BREACH_NOTIFICATION_MISSING: No process to notify Board and Data Principal of breach — Section 8(6)
_violation_flags_reference.CHILDREN_DATA_NO_PARENTAL_CONSENT: Child's data processed without verifiable parental consent — Section 9(1)
_violation_flags_reference.CHILDREN_DATA_PROFILING: Behavioural monitoring or targeted advertising directed at children — Section 9(3)
_violation_flags_reference.PURPOSE_UNKNOWN: Processing purpose cannot be determined from source context
_violation_flags_reference.NO_WITHDRAWAL_MECHANISM: No mechanism for Data Principal to withdraw consent — Section 6(4)
_violation_flags_reference.THIRD_PARTY_DISCLOSURE_RISK: Data sharing with third parties without adequate disclosure in notice — Section 5
_violation_flags_reference.CONSENT_NOT_SPECIFIC: Consent obtained for bundled purposes rather than specific purpose — Section 6(1)

AADHAAR.description: UIDAI-issued 12-digit unique identification number — a government identifier that constitutes personal data under Section 2(t). Highly sensitive in practice due to its universal use as a primary identity proof.
AADHAAR.note: DPDPA 2023 does not separately categorise Aadhaar beyond personal data. Aadhaar usage is additionally governed by the Aadhaar Act 2016 and UIDAI regulations. High sensitivity is operational, not a separate legal category under DPDPA.

recommended_actions: Ensure explicit consent is obtained before collecting Aadhaar — Section 6(1)
Provide clear notice stating Aadhaar is being collected and the specific purpose — Section 5
Implement strong encryption at rest and in transit — Section 8(4) and 8(5)
Establish and document data retention limit — delete after verification is complete — Section 8(7)
Implement data minimisation — collect only the Aadhaar, not unnecessary additional fields — Section 6(1)
Provide Data Principal with withdrawal mechanism — Section 6(4)
Establish grievance redressal mechanism — Section 8(10)
Implement breach notification process for Board and affected individuals — Section 8(6)
Note: Also verify compliance with Aadhaar Act 2016 and UIDAI regulations independently
Document the specific law or regulation that mandates Aadhaar collection — Section 7(d)
Provide notice even when processing under legitimate use basis — Section 5
Implement strong encryption at rest and in transit — Section 8(4) and 8(5)
Delete Aadhaar once regulatory obligation is fulfilled — Section 8(7)
Establish breach notification process — Section 8(6)
